prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian Regional Air Traffic Flow Management and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making System = Regional Flow Platform (Cedarbell); normalizes Flight Intent Message vs Airport Capacity Plan. TOBT (Target Off Block Time) proposed only if airside capacity and ground path allow; conditional if handling resources late; frozen at horizon unless rule exception/authorized override recorded. Airports Meridian International, Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport keep safety authority. Parts: Demand Prediction Service (Marlinstone); Capacity Assessment Module (CAM; demand vs Airport Acceptance Rate (AAR), runway configuration, taxiway, sectors; recalculates AAR; winter: cuts departure capacity for deicing, pad transit, slow taxi); Slot Allocation Engine (Blueharbor; derives CTT, Calculated Takeoff Time, within authority/fairness rules); Departure Metering Service (Emberline; TOBT protecting CTT; prefers stand absorption; sends CTT to TSM); North/South Runway Meter; Surface Surveillance Adapter; Airport CDM Portal (Foxglove; Common Situation Display; reconsideration requests); Tower Sequence Manager (TSM, Ironleaf); Gate Conflict Detector (warns stand holding blocking inbound/equipment move); Arrival Regulation Console; Sector Load Monitor; Alert Distribution Hub (Lantern; highlights runway queue over warning threshold on display); Ramp Movement Board (Skylark; Fuel Truck Hold Advice; states pending push, taxi to pad, in treatment, awaiting release, returning to stand); pad queue controls (assign deicing lane only once TOBT stable); Collaborative Decision Log and Audit Event Ledger (record all TOBT, CTT, threshold override changes); Performance Analytics Warehouse (verifies thresholds held); Handling Resource Planner (HRP); Weather Ingest Gateway (Orchard); Business Rules Registry (BRR; max planned runway queue, warning, intervention thresholds per runway configuration); Identity Access Service; Digital Briefing Room. Modes: Normal Operations; Adverse Weather Mode (Flow Manager may increase stand absorption)/Capacity Reduction State (Airport Duty Manager and Tower Supervisor agree metering horizon extension); Recovery Phase; Winter Operating Mode (freezing precipitation, contamination, low temperature; Capacity Plan gets winter margin before CTT recalculation). Actors: Regional Flow Manager (Copperfin); Slot Coordinator (Halcyon); Airline Operations Coordinator (AOC, Saffron; confirms stand delay absorbable); Aircraft Operator Representative (AOR; requests reconsideration); Ground Handling Dispatcher; Ramp Control Lead; Tower Supervisor; Airport Duty Manager; Meteorology Briefing

New part:
S378: Ramp Control Lead uses the queue card to verify pad entry order before authorizing a movement from the staging area.
S379: When demand exceeds the safe holding capacity near the pad, the Departure Metering Service withholds further push clearances until the pad queue falls below the configured threshold.
S380: The Tower Sequence Manager reserves departure sequence positions only for aircraft with an achievable pad release time and a valid runway taxi path.
S381: The Airport CDM Portal records the selected fluid type, mixture ratio, treatment start time, treatment completion time, and expected holdover reference for each treated aircraft.
S382: Fluid status updates are timestamped through the Time Synchronization Service so that ramp, tower, and airline users interpret treatment age consistently.
S383: The Ground Handling Dispatcher updates remaining fluid inventory and truck serviceability when replenishment, contamination, or equipment faults affect the planned treatment rate.
S384: The Handling Resource Planner compares fluid inventory with scheduled deicing demand and warns when a planned bank cannot be supported without resequencing.
S385: The Airline Operations Coordinator reviews aircraft readiness and may request a later pad entry when crew, catering, or passenger status would cause holdover time to be wasted.
S386: Gate Conflict Detector produces the Gate Reopening Memo when a stand becomes usable after snow clearance and the gate occupancy constraint has been removed.
S387: Quartzline must coordinate every pad release with the Tower Supervisor before the aircraft leaves the treated area.
S388: Under freezing conditions, the Tower Supervisor protects runway departure spacing by accounting for reduced braking action, slower lineup, and possible repeat treatment requests.
S389: The Surface Surveillance Adapter confirms that aircraft leaving the pad follow the assigned route and do not block inbound traffic to the same treatment complex.
S390: If a treated aircraft cannot depart within its applicable holdover reference, the Deicing Coordinator marks the treatment as expired and returns the aircraft to the appropriate queue state.
S391: The Common Situation Display highlights expired treatments, pad closures, fluid shortages, and ramp blockages so that participants can resolve conflicts without separate status calls.
S392: The Collaborative Decision Log captures winter-mode decisions, including capacity changes, pad flow restrictions, and agreed deviations from the normal departure order.
S393: When conditions improve, the Regional Flow Manager authorizes a controlled transition from Capacity Reduction State toward Recovery Phase after pad backlog, runway condition, and surface flow indicators are stable.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
